t: **Azure Monitor** is the dashboard of your car: it collects numbers and messages from everything and shows them. Two kinds of data: **metrics** are numbers measured at regular times (CPU 43%), **logs** are records with text (who signed in, which error).

**Azure Monitor** gaari ka dashboard hai: har cheez se numbers aur paigham jama kar ke dikhata hai. Do qism ka data: **metrics** waqfe waqfe se naape gaye numbers (CPU 43%), **logs** text wale records (kis ne sign in kiya, kaun sa error).
What is there without setup
Baghair setup kya milta hai

items: **Platform metrics**: for every resource, kept **93 days**, free. Seen in *Metrics explorer*.
**Platform metrics**: har resource ke, **93 din**, free. *Metrics explorer* mein.
**Activity log**: who created, changed or deleted which resource, kept **90 days**. Reads (GET) aren't in it.
**Activity log**: kis ne kaun sa resource banaya, badla ya delete kiya, **90 din**. Parhna (GET) is mein nahi.

t: Everything else you must switch on. **Resource logs** (what happened *inside* the resource, such as blob reads or Key Vault access) need a **diagnostic setting**, which sends them to one or more of: a **Log Analytics workspace** (to query), a **storage account** (cheap archive), an **event hub** (to other systems) or a partner solution. Up to five diagnostic settings per resource. The same setting keeps the activity log longer than 90 days.

Baqi sab khud on karna hai. **Resource logs** (resource ke *andar* kya hua, jaise blob parhna ya Key Vault access) ko **diagnostic setting** chahiye, jo unhein bhejti hai: **Log Analytics workspace** (query), **storage account** (sasta archive), **event hub** (doosre systems) ya partner solution. Har resource par paanch tak. Isi se activity log 90 din se zyada rehta hai.
Inside a VM
VM ke andar

Azure sees the CPU and the available memory from outside, but not **free disk space, processes, or the Windows event log**. Those live in the guest, so you install the **Azure Monitor Agent (AMA)** and tell it what to collect with a **data collection rule (DCR)**. One DCR can serve many VMs, and a VM can have several. The old Log Analytics agent (MMA) is retired.

Azure CPU aur available memory bahar se dekhta hai, lekin **disk ki khaali jagah, processes, ya Windows event log** nahi. Woh guest ke andar hain, is liye **Azure Monitor Agent (AMA)** lagayen aur **data collection rule (DCR)** se batayen kya jama ho. Ek DCR kai VMs ka, aur ek VM ke kai DCR. Purana Log Analytics agent (MMA) retire ho chuka.
Log Analytics workspace
Log Analytics workspace

The database for logs. Data comes into **tables**: `AzureActivity`, `Event` (Windows), `Syslog` (Linux), `Perf`, `Heartbeat`, `InsightsMetrics`, and resource tables such as `StorageBlobLogs`. You pay for data **coming in** and for long storage. Interactive retention is 30 days by default, up to 730, and total retention up to **12 years**. Table plans: **Analytics** (full features), **Basic** (cheaper in, pay per query) and **Auxiliary** (cheapest, for audit). A **daily cap** stops collection at a limit, which also makes you blind for the rest of the day. Access is by workspace, or by resource: someone with rights on a VM may see only that VM's logs.

Logs ka database. Data **tables** mein: `AzureActivity`, `Event` (Windows), `Syslog` (Linux), `Perf`, `Heartbeat`, `InsightsMetrics`, aur resource tables jaise `StorageBlobLogs`. Paisa **aane wale** data aur lambi storage ka. Interactive retention default 30 din, 730 tak, kul **12 saal** tak. Table plans: **Analytics** (poore features), **Basic** (aana sasta, query ka paisa) aur **Auxiliary** (sab se sasta, audit ke liye). **Daily cap** hadd par collection rok deta hai, phir baqi din kuch nahi dikhta. Access workspace se, ya resource se: jis ka VM par haq hai woh sirf us VM ke logs dekhe.
KQL in ten minutes
Das minute mein KQL
A query starts with a table, and the **pipe** `|` hands the rows to the next step. Read it top to bottom like a sentence:
Query table se shuru hoti hai, aur **pipe** `|` rows agle step ko deta hai. Upar se neeche jumle ki tarah parhein:

items: `where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)` keeps rows. Put it first: less data, faster query.
`where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)` rows rakhta hai. Pehle likhein: kam data, tez query.
`project Computer, RenderedDescription` chooses columns; `extend` adds a computed one.
`project Computer, RenderedDescription` columns chunta hai; `extend` naya banata hai.
`summarize count() by Computer` groups; `avg()`, `max()`, `dcount()` are other functions.
`summarize count() by Computer` group; `avg()`, `max()`, `dcount()` doosre functions.
`bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)` makes time steps for a chart; `render timechart` draws it.
`bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)` chart ke waqt ke hisse; `render timechart` chart.
`top 10 by X`, `sort by X desc`, `take 5` (any five rows), `distinct Computer`.
`top 10 by X`, `sort by X desc`, `take 5` (koi paanch rows), `distinct Computer`.
`search "error"` looks in all tables, slowly. `has` finds whole words and is faster than `contains`.
`search "error"` tamam tables mein, slow. `has` poore lafz, `contains` se tez.

t: Errors per computer in the last day: `Event | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) | where EventLevelName == "Error" | summarize n = count() by Computer | top 10 by n`. Machines that have gone silent: `Heartbeat | summarize last = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where last < ago(5m)`.

Pichle din har computer ke errors: `Event | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) | where EventLevelName == "Error" | summarize n = count() by Computer | top 10 by n`. Khamosh machines: `Heartbeat | summarize last = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where last < ago(5m)`.
Monitor → Metrics / Logs / Activity log / Data Collection Rules · Resource → Monitoring → Diagnostic settings · Log Analytics workspaces
Monitor → Metrics / Logs / Activity log / Data Collection Rules · Resource → Monitoring → Diagnostic settings · Log Analytics workspaces
*Free disk space of a VM* doesn't come from a platform metric or a diagnostic setting. It's **AMA + DCR**.
*VM ki disk ki khaali jagah* platform metric ya diagnostic setting se nahi milti. **AMA + DCR** hai.
Who deleted the resource group 120 days ago? Activity log was never exported.
120 din pehle resource group kis ne delete kiya? Activity log export nahi tha.
a: You can't see it: the activity log goes back 90 days.
Nahi dikhega: activity log 90 din ka hai.

t: What sends Key Vault access logs to a workspace?
Key Vault ke access logs workspace mein kaise?
a: A diagnostic setting on the vault.
Vault par diagnostic setting.

t: What does `| take 10` return?
`| take 10` kya deta hai?
a: Any 10 rows, in no guaranteed order. Use top for the highest.
Koi bhi 10 rows, tarteeb yaqeeni nahi. Sab se bare ke liye top.

t: A dashboard helps only when you look at it. An **alert** looks for you. Every alert has three parts: the **alert rule** (what to watch and when it's bad), the **action group** (whom to tell or what to do) and, optionally, **alert processing rules** (exceptions, such as maintenance).

Dashboard tabhi kaam aata hai jab dekhein. **Alert** aap ki jagah dekhta hai. Teen hisse: **alert rule** (kya dekhna hai aur kab kharab), **action group** (kis ko batana ya kya karna) aur, chahein to, **alert processing rules** (istisna, jaise maintenance).
Kinds of alert rules
Alert rules ki qismein

items: **Metric alert**: a number crosses a limit, e.g. CPU > 80% for 5 minutes. Fast. *Static* threshold, or *dynamic*, which learns what is normal.
**Metric alert**: number hadd paar kare, maslan CPU 5 minute 80% se upar. Tez. *Static* threshold, ya *dynamic* jo mamool seekhta hai.
**Log search alert**: a KQL query finds rows, e.g. more than 5 errors in 10 minutes.
**Log search alert**: KQL query rows dhoonde, maslan 10 minute mein 5 se zyada errors.
**Activity log alert**: someone did something, e.g. a VM was deleted. Includes **Service health** and **Resource health** alerts.
**Activity log alert**: kisi ne kuch kiya, maslan VM delete. **Service health** aur **Resource health** alerts bhi isi mein.

t: How do you choose? *A number of the platform* → metric. *Text, several tables or guest data in a workspace* → log search. *Somebody changed a resource* → activity log. *Azure itself has a problem in my region* → Service health alert. *My one VM is unavailable because of the platform* → Resource health alert.

Kaise chunein? *Platform ka number* → metric. *Text, kai tables ya workspace mein guest data* → log search. *Kisi ne resource badla* → activity log. *Azure mein hi mere region mein masla* → Service health. *Meri ek VM platform ki wajah se band* → Resource health.
Details of a rule
Rule ki tafseel

The **scope** is the resource, or for some types a whole group or subscription. The **condition** has a signal, an aggregation (average, maximum, count), a **lookback period** (how much data) and a **frequency** (how often it's checked). **Severity** goes from **0 (critical) to 4 (verbose)**. A *stateful* metric alert fires once and *resolves* by itself when the value is normal again. The *user response* (New, Acknowledged, Closed) is set by people and is separate from *Fired/Resolved*. Fired alerts are kept 30 days.

**Scope** resource hai, kuch qismon mein poora group ya subscription. **Condition** mein signal, aggregation (average, maximum, count), **lookback period** (kitna data) aur **frequency** (kitni dafa check). **Severity** **0 (critical) se 4 (verbose)**. *Stateful* metric alert ek dafa fire hota hai aur value theek hone par khud *resolve*. *User response* (New, Acknowledged, Closed) log set karte hain aur *Fired/Resolved* se alag hai. Alerts 30 din rehte hain.
Action groups
Action groups

A reusable list of **notifications** (email, SMS, voice, app push, or email to a role such as Owner) and **actions** (Automation runbook, Azure Function, Logic App, webhook, ITSM, event hub). One action group can serve many rules, and a rule can use up to five. Rate limits protect people: one SMS per 5 minutes per number, one voice call per 5 minutes, at most 100 emails an hour per address. Use **Test action group** to check it before you need it.

**Notifications** (email, SMS, voice, app push, ya Owner jaise role ko email) aur **actions** (Automation runbook, Azure Function, Logic App, webhook, ITSM, event hub) ki dobara use hone wali list. Ek action group kai rules ka, aur ek rule mein paanch tak. Hadein: ek number par 5 minute mein ek SMS, 5 minute mein ek call, ek address par ghante mein 100 emails tak. Zaroorat se pehle **Test action group** se check karein.
Alert processing rules
Alert processing rules

They change what happens to alerts that fire, without touching the rules. **Suppress notifications** during the maintenance on Saturday from 22 to 2 (once or recurring), or **apply an action group** to every alert of a scope. While suppressed, alerts still *fire* and can be seen; only the actions are silent.

Fire hone wale alerts ke sath kya ho yeh badalte hain, rules chhere baghair. Hafte ki raat 22 se 2 maintenance mein **notifications suppress** (ek dafa ya baar baar), ya scope ke har alert par **action group lagana**. Suppress mein alert *fire* hota hai aur dikhta hai; sirf actions khamosh.
Every Sunday you restart 40 VMs and 40 people get emails. Don't disable the 40 alert rules: create one alert processing rule on the resource group, suppress, recurring on Sundays.
Har Itwar 40 VMs restart hoti hain aur 40 logon ko email. 40 rules band na karein: resource group par ek alert processing rule, suppress, har Itwar.
Monitor → Alerts → Create (alert rule, action group, alert processing rule) · Service Health → Health alerts
Monitor → Alerts → Create (alert rule, action group, alert processing rule) · Service Health → Health alerts
An alert without an action group fires and tells nobody.
Action group ke baghair alert fire hota hai aur kisi ko nahi batata.
Notify when someone deletes a VM. Which type?
VM delete hone par batana hai. Kaun si qism?
a: An activity log alert.
Activity log alert.

t: Which severity is the worst?
Sab se kharab severity?
a: 0, critical.
0, critical.

t: An alert fires but no email arrives. Name three things to check.
Alert fire hua lekin email nahi. Teen cheezein?
a: Is there an action group, is the address right and confirmed (Test action group), and is an alert processing rule suppressing it?
Action group laga hai, address sahi hai (Test action group), aur koi alert processing rule suppress to nahi kar raha?

t: **Insights** are ready-made views: instead of building charts and queries yourself, you open a page made for that kind of resource. **Network Watcher** does the same for networks.
**Insights** bane banaye views hain: charts aur queries khud banane ki jagah us qism ke resource ka page kholein. **Network Watcher** network ke liye yehi karta hai.
VM insights
VM insights

Shows CPU, memory, disk and network of one VM or of all. You turn it on from *Insights* on the VM; it installs the **Azure Monitor Agent** and a **data collection rule**, and the data goes to a Log Analytics workspace. The **Map** with processes and connections (Dependency agent) is being retired: 30 June 2028. To enable it on many VMs, use Azure Policy.

Ek ya tamam VMs ka CPU, memory, disk aur network. VM ke *Insights* se on karein; **Azure Monitor Agent** aur **data collection rule** lagta hai, data Log Analytics workspace mein. Processes aur connections wala **Map** (Dependency agent) retire ho raha hai: 30 June 2028. Bohat si VMs par Azure Policy se.
The other insights
Baqi insights

items: **Storage insights**: capacity, latency, availability and requests of all storage accounts, no setup.
**Storage insights**: tamam storage accounts ki capacity, latency, availability aur requests, setup nahi.
**Network insights**: health of load balancers, gateways, VNets in one place, no setup.
**Network insights**: load balancers, gateways, VNets ki health ek jagah, setup nahi.
**Container insights**, **Key Vault insights**, **Log Analytics workspace insights** (who sends so much data?).
**Container insights**, **Key Vault insights**, **Log Analytics workspace insights** (itna data kaun bhej raha hai?).
**Application Insights**: for your app's code: requests, failures, dependencies, users. Not on the AZ-104 outline, but good to recognize.
**Application Insights**: app ke code ke liye: requests, failures, dependencies, users. AZ-104 outline mein nahi, pehchanna achha hai.

t: Metrics explorer, dashboards and workbooks
Metrics explorer, dashboards aur workbooks

In **Metrics explorer** you pick the resource, the metric and the aggregation. **Split** shows one line per value of a dimension (for example per API name); **filter** keeps only some. Pin the chart to a **dashboard** for a quick look, or build a **workbook** for a report with text, parameters and queries. **Azure Managed Grafana** is a third choice.

**Metrics explorer** mein resource, metric aur aggregation chunein. **Split** dimension ki har value ki alag line (maslan API name); **filter** sirf kuch rakhta hai. Chart **dashboard** par pin karein, ya text, parameters aur queries wali report ke liye **workbook**. **Azure Managed Grafana** teesra intikhab.
Choose the aggregation with care. *Average* CPU of 40% can hide a *maximum* of 100%. For counts use *sum*.
Aggregation soch kar chunein. *Average* CPU 40% mein *maximum* 100% chhup sakta hai. Ginti ke liye *sum*.
Network Watcher
Network Watcher

It's enabled per region when you have a VNet there. Three groups of tools. **Monitoring**: Topology, Connection monitor. **Diagnostics**: IP flow verify, NSG diagnostics, Next hop, Effective security rules, Connection troubleshoot, Packet capture, VPN troubleshoot. **Traffic**: flow logs and Traffic Analytics.

Region mein VNet ho to wahan on hota hai. Tools ke teen group. **Monitoring**: Topology, Connection monitor. **Diagnostics**: IP flow verify, NSG diagnostics, Next hop, Effective security rules, Connection troubleshoot, Packet capture, VPN troubleshoot. **Traffic**: flow logs aur Traffic Analytics.

**Connection monitor** runs tests all the time between sources (VMs, scale sets, on-premises machines with the Arc agent) and destinations (VM, URL, IP), reports reachability and round-trip time, and can raise alerts. A *test group* joins sources, destinations and *test configurations* (protocol, port, interval, thresholds).

**Connection monitor** sources (VMs, scale sets, Arc agent wali on-premises machines) aur destinations (VM, URL, IP) ke darmiyan hamesha test chalata hai, reachability aur round-trip time batata hai, aur alert de sakta hai. *Test group* sources, destinations aur *test configurations* (protocol, port, interval, thresholds) jorta hai.

**VNet flow logs** record the traffic of a VNet, subnet or NIC to a **storage account** in the same region. **Traffic Analytics** reads them into a Log Analytics workspace and shows top talkers, blocked traffic and countries. They need only a VNet, no NSG. NSG flow logs can't be created any more and retire on 30 September 2027: migrate.

**VNet flow logs** VNet, subnet ya NIC ka traffic usi region ke **storage account** mein likhte hain. **Traffic Analytics** unhein Log Analytics workspace mein parh kar sab se zyada baat karne wale, blocked traffic aur mulk dikhata hai. Sirf VNet chahiye, NSG nahi. NSG flow logs naye nahi bante aur 30 September 2027 ko retire: migrate karein.

'The application between VM1 and an on-premises server is slow every evening.' Connection troubleshoot at noon shows nothing. Set up Connection monitor, wait a day, and read the round-trip time of the evening.
'VM1 aur on-premises server ke darmiyan app har shaam slow hai.' Dopahar ka connection troubleshoot kuch nahi dikhata. Connection monitor lagayen, ek din rukein, shaam ka round-trip time parhein.
Monitor → Insights (Virtual Machines, Storage accounts, Networks) · Monitor → Workbooks · Network Watcher
Monitor → Insights (Virtual Machines, Storage accounts, Networks) · Monitor → Workbooks · Network Watcher
Connection **troubleshoot** is one test now. Connection **monitor** is continuous. The word 'over time' decides.
Connection **troubleshoot** abhi ka ek test. Connection **monitor** lagatar. 'Over time' lafz faisla karta hai.
Where do VNet flow logs go first?
VNet flow logs pehle kahan jate hain?
a: To a storage account in the same region.
Usi region ke storage account mein.

t: You want latency split by API name for a storage account. Where?
Storage account ki latency API name ke hisab se. Kahan?
a: Metrics explorer, apply splitting on the API name dimension.
Metrics explorer, API name dimension par splitting.

t: What does VM insights install?
VM insights kya lagata hai?
a: The Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule.
Azure Monitor Agent, data collection rule ke sath.

t: A backup is a copy from **before** the mistake, kept where the mistake can't reach it. **Azure Backup** makes the copies, keeps them by rules and restores them. Two words to know: **RPO** is how much data you may lose (time since the last copy), **RTO** is how long the restore may take.

Backup ghalti se **pehle** ki copy hai, aisi jagah jahan ghalti na pahunche. **Azure Backup** copies banata, rules se rakhta aur restore karta hai. Do lafz: **RPO** kitna data khona qabool (aakhri copy se ab tak), **RTO** restore mein kitna waqt.
Two kinds of vault
Do qism ke vault

items: **Recovery Services vault**: Azure VMs, SQL and SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files, on-premises (MARS agent, MABS). Also Site Recovery.
**Recovery Services vault**: Azure VMs, VM mein SQL aur SAP HANA, Azure Files, on-premises (MARS agent, MABS). Site Recovery bhi.
**Backup vault**: the newer kind, for blobs, managed disks, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes and other newer workloads.
**Backup vault**: naya, blobs, managed disks, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes aur doosre naye workloads.

t: The vault must be in the **same region** as what it protects (the resource group may differ). Decide its redundancy **before the first backup**: GRS is the default, LRS or ZRS cost less; afterwards it can't be changed. **Cross Region Restore** needs GRS. A vault that contains backup items, also soft-deleted ones, can't be deleted: stop the backups and delete the data first.

Vault **usi region** mein jis mein resource (resource group alag ho sakta hai). Redundancy **pehle backup se pehle** tay karein: default GRS, LRS ya ZRS sasti; baad mein nahi badalti. **Cross Region Restore** ko GRS chahiye. Jis vault mein backup items hon, soft-deleted bhi, delete nahi hota: pehle backups rok kar data delete karein.
Backup policy
Backup policy

A policy is **schedule + retention**. The **Standard** policy backs up a VM once a day (or weekly); the **Enhanced** policy every 4 to 24 hours and supports Trusted launch VMs. Retention can be daily, weekly, monthly and yearly (grandfather, father, son). **Instant restore** keeps a snapshot next to the VM for some days (1–5 with Standard, up to 30 with Enhanced), so a recent restore is fast; then the data sits in the vault. Changing the policy affects **existing recovery points too**, if retention is shortened or lengthened.

Policy **schedule + retention** hai. **Standard** VM ka din mein ek (ya hafte war); **Enhanced** har 4 se 24 ghante aur Trusted launch VMs support. Retention daily, weekly, monthly aur yearly. **Instant restore** VM ke paas kuch din snapshot rakhta hai (Standard 1–5, Enhanced 30 tak), taza restore tez; phir data vault mein. Policy ki retention badlein to **mojooda recovery points par bhi** asar hota hai.

The first backup is full, later ones incremental. A VM's copy is **application-consistent** on Windows through VSS, **file-system consistent** on Linux by default, and **crash-consistent** if the VM is off.
Pehla backup full, baad ke incremental. VM ki copy Windows par VSS se **application-consistent**, Linux par default **file-system consistent**, aur VM band ho to **crash-consistent**.
Restoring
Restore

items: **Create a new VM**: quick, basic settings.
**Create a new VM**: jaldi, basic settings.
**Restore disks**: you get the disks (and a template) and build the VM as you like: other size, availability set, network.
**Restore disks**: disks (aur template) milti hain, VM apni marzi ki banayen: doosra size, availability set, network.
**Replace existing**: swaps the disks of the existing VM. The VM must exist; current disks are kept as a backup first.
**Replace existing**: mojooda VM ki disks badalta hai. VM maujood ho; pehle mojooda disks backup hoti hain.
**File recovery**: mounts the recovery point with a script for **12 hours**, so you copy single files.
**File recovery**: script se recovery point **12 ghante** mount, akeli files copy karein.
**Cross region**: restore in the paired region.
**Cross region**: paired region mein restore.

t: Protecting the backups
Backups ki hifazat

An attacker deletes backups first. **Soft delete** keeps deleted backups for at least 14 days (14 to 180) and can't be switched off any more. **Immutable vault** forbids shortening; once *locked* it can't be undone. **Multi-user authorization** with a Resource Guard asks a second person for dangerous operations. Roles: **Backup Contributor** (all except deleting the vault and giving access), **Backup Operator** (no policy changes, no removing), **Backup Reader**.

Hamla karne wala pehle backups delete karta hai. **Soft delete** delete hui backups kam se kam 14 din rakhta hai (14 se 180) aur ab band nahi hota. **Immutable vault** kam karne se rokta hai; *lock* ke baad wapas nahi. **Multi-user authorization** (Resource Guard) khatarnak kaam par doosre shakhs ki ijazat. Roles: **Backup Contributor** (vault delete aur access dene ke siwa sab), **Backup Operator** (policy badalna aur backup hatana nahi), **Backup Reader**.
Files and on-premises
Files aur on-premises

**Azure Files**: snapshot-based backups in the same storage account, or *vaulted* backups in the vault. **MARS agent**: files and folders of a Windows machine; install, register with the **vault credentials**, and choose a **passphrase**. Microsoft can't recover it: lose the passphrase and the backups are useless. **MABS/DPM**: servers and applications on-premises.

**Azure Files**: usi storage account mein snapshot backups, ya vault mein *vaulted*. **MARS agent**: Windows machine ki files aur folders; install, **vault credentials** se register, aur **passphrase** chunein. Microsoft usay wapas nahi la sakta: gum ho to backups bekaar. **MABS/DPM**: on-premises servers aur applications.
Reports and watching
Reports aur nigrani

**Resiliency** (formerly the Azure Business Continuity Center) shows all vaults, jobs and unprotected resources in one place. **Backup reports** need a diagnostic setting from the vault to a **Log Analytics workspace**; data appears after up to 24 hours. Alerts for failed jobs go through Azure Monitor.

**Resiliency** (pehle Azure Business Continuity Center) tamam vaults, jobs aur baghair backup resources ek jagah. **Backup reports** ko vault se **Log Analytics workspace** tak diagnostic setting chahiye; data 24 ghante tak mein. Fail jobs ke alerts Azure Monitor se.
A user deleted a folder on a VM two weeks ago. Not a whole restore: choose the recovery point from before, *File recovery*, run the script, copy the folder, unmount.
User ne do hafte pehle VM ka folder delete kiya. Poora restore nahi: us se pehle ka recovery point, *File recovery*, script chalayen, folder copy, unmount.
Recovery Services vault → Backup / Backup items / Backup policies / Properties · Virtual machine → Backup · Resiliency
Recovery Services vault → Backup / Backup items / Backup policies / Properties · Virtual machine → Backup · Resiliency
Vault in West Europe, VM in North Europe: you won't even see the VM in the list. Same region, always.
Vault West Europe, VM North Europe: VM list mein dikhegi hi nahi. Hamesha ek hi region.
Which vault for Azure Files, and which for blobs?
Azure Files ke liye kaun sa vault, blobs ke liye kaun sa?
a: Files: Recovery Services vault. Blobs: Backup vault.
Files: Recovery Services vault. Blobs: Backup vault.

t: A VM needs a backup every 4 hours. What do you use?
VM ka backup har 4 ghante. Kya use karein?
a: An Enhanced policy.
Enhanced policy.

t: The vault was created with LRS and has backups. You want Cross Region Restore. What now?
Vault LRS par hai aur backups hain. Cross Region Restore chahiye. Ab?
a: Create a new vault with GRS, and protect the items there.
GRS ke sath naya vault banayen aur items wahan protect karein.

t: Backup answers *'I deleted something'*. **Azure Site Recovery (ASR)** answers *'the whole region (or my datacenter) is down'*. It copies your machines **all the time** to another place, so you can start them there within minutes.

Backup ka sawal *'main ne kuch delete kar diya'*. **Azure Site Recovery (ASR)** ka *'poora region (ya mera datacenter) band hai'*. Aap ki machines ko **har waqt** doosri jagah copy karta hai, taa ke minuton mein wahan chalayen.
What can be replicated
Kya replicate hota hai

items: Azure VM → another Azure **region**, or another **zone** of the same region.
Azure VM → doosra Azure **region**, ya usi region ka doosra **zone**.
On-premises VMware, Hyper-V and physical servers → Azure.
On-premises VMware, Hyper-V aur physical servers → Azure.

t: For Azure to Azure, the **Recovery Services vault must be in the target region** (or any region except the source), because the source may be gone when you need it. Compare: for Backup the vault is in the *same* region as the VM. This difference is a favourite exam question.

Azure se Azure mein **Recovery Services vault target region mein ho** (ya source ke siwa kisi bhi region mein), kyunke zaroorat ke waqt source ghayab ho sakta hai. Muqabla: Backup mein vault VM ke *usi* region mein. Yeh farq exam ka pasandeeda sawal hai.
How it works
Kaise chalta hai

When you enable replication, Azure installs the **Mobility service** on the VM. Disk writes go to a **cache storage account** in the source region and from there to disks in the target region. The target VM doesn't exist yet, so you don't pay for its compute, only for storage, the ASR licence per VM and the traffic. The target network, subnets, size and availability options are chosen in advance and can be edited. **Outbound HTTPS** from the VM must be allowed.

Replication on karne par Azure VM par **Mobility service** lagata hai. Disk writes source region ke **cache storage account** mein, phir target region ki disks mein. Target VM abhi bani nahi hoti, is liye compute ka paisa nahi, sirf storage, har VM ka ASR licence aur traffic. Target network, subnets, size aur availability pehle chune jate hain aur badal sakte hain. VM se **outbound HTTPS** allow ho.
Recovery points and policy
Recovery points aur policy

A **crash-consistent** point every **5 minutes** (the disk as if the power went off), kept up to 15 days for managed disks. **Application-consistent** points (memory and pending writes too) are off by default; you set their frequency in hours. When you fail over, choose: *Latest* (lowest RPO), *Latest processed* (lowest RTO), *Latest app-consistent*, or *Custom*.

**Crash-consistent** point har **5 minute** (jaise bijli chali gayi), managed disks ke liye 15 din tak. **Application-consistent** (memory aur ruki hui writes bhi) default off; waqfa ghanton mein. Failover mein chunein: *Latest* (kam RPO), *Latest processed* (kam RTO), *Latest app-consistent*, ya *Custom*.
Three kinds of failover
Failover ki teen qismein

items: **Test failover**: a drill into an **isolated VNet**. Production and replication go on. Afterwards *Cleanup test failover*.
**Test failover**: **alag VNet** mein mashq. Production aur replication chalte rehte hain. Baad mein *Cleanup test failover*.
**Failover**: the real thing. Option to shut the source down first, so the last changes are copied. Then **Commit** (after that you can't choose another point).
**Failover**: asal. Pehle source band karne ka option, taa ke aakhri tabdeeliyan copy hon. Phir **Commit** (us ke baad doosra point nahi chun sakte).
**Planned failover** (Hyper-V to Azure): no data loss, source is shut down first.
**Planned failover** (Hyper-V se Azure): data ka nuqsan nahi, source pehle band.

t: After a failover the new VMs are **not protected**. Run **Re-protect**: replication turns around. When the old region is healthy, fail over again (that's **failback**) and re-protect once more. The order to remember: *Failover → Commit → Re-protect → Failback → Re-protect*.

Failover ke baad nayi VMs **protected nahi**. **Re-protect** chalayen: replication ulti simt. Purana region theek ho to dobara failover (yehi **failback**) aur phir re-protect. Tarteeb: *Failover → Commit → Re-protect → Failback → Re-protect*.
Recovery plans
Recovery plans

A **recovery plan** starts machines in order: group 1 databases, group 2 application, group 3 web. Between the groups you add **Automation runbooks** (for example change DNS) or **manual actions** (call the manager). Use the plan for tests, so the drill is the same as the emergency.

**Recovery plan** machines tarteeb se chalata hai: group 1 databases, group 2 application, group 3 web. Groups ke darmiyan **Automation runbooks** (maslan DNS badalna) ya **manual actions** (manager ko call). Test bhi isi plan se, taa ke mashq aur emergency ek jaisi hon.

What doesn't come along automatically: the IP address changes unless the target subnet has the same range and you set it, and load balancers, public IPs and NSGs must be prepared or attached by script.
Jo khud nahi aata: IP address badalta hai jab tak target subnet ki range wahi na ho aur set na karein, aur load balancers, public IPs aur NSG tayyar rakhne ya script se lagane hote hain.
Backup or Site Recovery
Backup ya Site Recovery

items: Deleted file, ransomware, 'give me last March' → **Backup**. Keeps years.
Delete hui file, ransomware, 'pichla March do' → **Backup**. Saalon rakhta hai.
Region or datacenter outage, run again in minutes → **Site Recovery**. Keeps days.
Region ya datacenter band, minuton mein chalao → **Site Recovery**. Dinon rakhta hai.
They complement each other, and a VM can have both.
Dono ek doosre ke sath hain, VM par dono ho sakte hain.

t: VM in West Europe, disaster target North Europe: backup vault in West Europe, ASR vault in North Europe. Every half year: test failover into an empty VNet in North Europe, check the application, clean up.
VM West Europe, disaster target North Europe: backup vault West Europe mein, ASR vault North Europe mein. Har chhe mahine: North Europe ke khaali VNet mein test failover, app check, cleanup.
Virtual machine → Disaster recovery · Recovery Services vault → Replicated items / Recovery Plans (Site Recovery) / Site Recovery infrastructure
Virtual machine → Disaster recovery · Recovery Services vault → Replicated items / Recovery Plans (Site Recovery) / Site Recovery infrastructure
A deleted or encrypted file is replicated to the target as well. ASR doesn't replace backup.
Delete ya encrypt hui file target mein bhi replicate hoti hai. ASR backup ki jagah nahi.
Where is the vault for Azure-to-Azure replication?
Azure-to-Azure replication ka vault kahan?
a: Not in the source region; usually in the target region.
Source region mein nahi; aam tor par target region mein.

t: A test failover is finished. What is the last step?
Test failover mukammal. Aakhri qadam?
a: Cleanup test failover, which deletes the test VMs.
Cleanup test failover, jo test VMs delete karta hai.

t: After a failover, what makes the VMs protected again?
Failover ke baad VMs dobara protected kaise?
a: Re-protect.
Re-protect.
